title: Governor of Illinois

context.text: Incumbent Democrat JB Pritzker is seeking a third term.

The Illinois State Board of Elections candidate list shows three active governor/lieutenant governor tickets for Nov. 3: Pritzker–Mitchell (Democratic), Bailey–Del Mar (Republican) and Corbett–Schofield (Independent). Green, Independence Party and New Party filings were removed.
Pritzker was unopposed in the Democratic primary after challenger Patricia Tillman was disqualified.
Darren Bailey, the 2022 Republican nominee, won the Republican primary with 53.3%, ahead of Ted Dabrowski (28.9%), James Mendrick (9.6%) and Rick Heidner (8.1%).
Independent Collin Corbett is also running; a Public Policy Polling survey conducted Sept. 30–Oct. 1 showed him at 6%.

candidates.name: JB Pritzker
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Christian Mitchell, a former deputy governor and state representative. Unopposed in the Democratic primary.

summary.text: JB Pritzker is the incumbent Governor of Illinois, seeking a third term. A businessman before entering office, he was first elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. As governor he signed a phase-in of a $15 minimum wage, an assault-weapons ban, abortion-rights and immigrant-protection laws, and created a Department of Early Childhood.

background.text: Earned a B.A. from Duke University (1987) and a J.D. from Northwestern University; worked on Capitol Hill staffs for Rep. Tom Lantos and Sen. Alan Dixon.
Co-founded Pritzker Group Private Capital with his brother Anthony and served as managing partner until 2017.
Elected governor in 2018, defeating incumbent Republican Bruce Rauner, and re-elected in 2022, defeating Darren Bailey.

priorities.text: Raising wages, attracting businesses and creating jobs, and taking on corporations driving up costs, per the campaign site.
Protecting what the campaign site calls 'your most fundamental freedoms'; as governor he signed abortion-rights and immigrant-protection laws.
Early childhood programs, including the Department of Early Childhood he proposed in October 2023 and signed into law in 2024.

positions.summary: Signed SB 1 in 2019 phasing in a $15 minimum wage over six years.
Signed HB 370 in 2021 repealing the Parental Notification Act for abortion.
Signed laws in 2021 strengthening the TRUST Act and requiring local officials to end partnerships with ICE.
Signed the Protect Illinois Communities Act in January 2023, banning the sale of assault weapons and high-capacity magazines.
Championed a 2020 constitutional amendment to allow a graduated income tax (which he called a 'fair tax') with higher rates on higher incomes; voters rejected it in November 2020.
positions.quote: For years, Illinoisans have been fighting to make our income tax system more fair to middle class families and those striving to get there, and this monumental vote in the General Assembly means that voters will have the right to decide our system for themselves in November 2020

record.text: Signed SB 1, phasing in a $15 minimum wage in Illinois over six years.
Signed HB 121, SB 667, SB 1596 and SB 2665 expanding protections for immigrant and refugee communities and issued an executive order establishing the Welcoming Illinois Office.
Signed HB 370, repealing the Parental Notification Act.
Signed the Protect Illinois Communities Act, banning the sale and distribution of assault weapons, high-capacity magazines and switches.
Signed SB 1, creating the Illinois Department of Early Childhood.
Signed SB 3365, the Medicaid omnibus bill, with hospital financial reforms and long-term care standards.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Aaron Del Mar, Cook County Republican Party chair. Won the March Republican primary with 53.3%.

summary.text: Darren Bailey is a southern Illinois farmer, former state representative (2019–2021) and state senator (2021–2023), and the Republican nominee for governor for the second time; he lost to JB Pritzker in 2022. His campaign focuses on property taxes, utility costs, public safety and education.

background.text: Third-generation farmer from Louisville, Illinois; earned an associate degree in agricultural production from Lake Land College.
Served on the North Clay Board of Education for 17 years, including 12 as president; he and his wife founded a private Christian school.
Elected to the Illinois House in 2018 and the Illinois Senate in 2020, where he was Republican spokesperson on the Agriculture Committee.

priorities.text: Lowering taxes, especially property taxes, and cutting government spending.
Restoring public safety and standing with law enforcement.
Education and parental choices for children.

positions.summary: As a state senator filed legislation in April 2021 to eliminate the state's FOID card program; also reported as signing onto a bill letting active-military applicants under 18 buy firearms without parental consent.
positions.quote: It’s time to void the FOID and restore people’s God-given constitutional rights.

positions.summary: Says he holds anti-abortion personal views but would not push legislation to advance them if elected.

record.text: Voted against the SAFE-T Act, the criminal justice package that abolished cash bail.
Voted against legalizing recreational cannabis and more casinos.

Chief sponsor in the Senate of one bill that became law to help recruit firefighters; as a House member, primary sponsor of just one enacted law, which increased fines for illegally passing school buses.
Sued Gov. Pritzker in April 2020 over the extension of his COVID-19 stay-at-home order; a judge granted a temporary restraining order that applied to Bailey only.

candidates.researchNotes: Vote items come from a WBEZ/IPM news report that does not give dates, so none are shown. Official ILGA roll-call pages could not be reached from this environment; the repo snapshots cover only the current session, in which Bailey did not serve. April 2020 lawsuit has no day-level date in the cited source.

candidates.name: Collin Corbett
candidates.ballotNote: Running as an independent with Lt. Gov. candidate Carolyn Schofield, a former Republican candidate for lieutenant governor.

summary.text: Collin Corbett is a political strategist and small-business owner and a former Republican campaign strategist who is running for governor as an independent. His platform emphasizes affordability, including tax changes, and fixing the Department of Children and Family Services; he says he wants to bring more balance to the race.

background.text: Founded Cor Strategies, EmpowerPolitics and Long9 Studio; says he has recruited and trained over 3,500 people to participate in politics.
Filed to run for governor as an independent in May 2026 after a career as a Republican campaign strategist.

priorities.text: Making life more affordable, including property, sales and income tax changes.
Fixing the Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS), which his platform calls a top priority.

positions.summary: His platform says the state's flat income tax is 'necessary in Illinois under the current leadership' and opposes giving politicians power to raise income taxes on targeted groups, while proposing larger earned-income and child tax credits.
positions.quote: Politicians have proven they cannot be trusted with the power to raise income taxes on targeted groups, a power they would abuse on an annual basis as they continue to struggle to balance their budgets.

positions.summary: Proposes reducing mandates and permitting delays, impact-fee transparency, matching grants for local zoning and planning updates, and an opt-in permitting program for local governments that includes one for 'missing middle' housing, while preserving local control.

candidates.researchNotes: Read his campaign platform page in full. Two stances (taxes, housing) were already recorded; added statements on energy and child care. The platform does not take a side on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, minimum wage or school choice.

statements.quote: We will bring down energy costs and restore reliability while moving into our clean energy future.
statements.context: On his campaign platform page, Energy section

statements.quote: We will increase access to childcare, lower costs, and raise wages for families.
statements.context: On his campaign platform page, Affordability section
